heading.en: Why the J must bend into an S

hook.en: No pond has unlimited food or space. As a population fills its habitat, growth slows and levels off at the number the habitat can support.
hook.kn: ಯಾವ ಕೊಳದಲ್ಲೂ ಅಪರಿಮಿತ ಆಹಾರ ಅಥವಾ ಸ್ಥಳ ಇರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸಮಷ್ಟಿ ತನ್ನ ಆವಾಸವನ್ನು ತುಂಬುತ್ತಿದ್ದಂತೆ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ, ಆವಾಸವು ಪೋಷಿಸಬಲ್ಲ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

objectives.en: Explain carrying capacity and the logistic growth equation
Identify the phases of a sigmoid curve
Describe life history variations among organisms

narration.en: No pond has unlimited food or space. As a population fills its habitat, growth slows and levels off at the number the habitat can support.
narration.kn: ಯಾವ ಕೊಳದಲ್ಲೂ ಅಪರಿಮಿತ ಆಹಾರ ಅಥವಾ ಸ್ಥಳ ಇರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸಮಷ್ಟಿ ತನ್ನ ಆವಾಸವನ್ನು ತುಂಬುತ್ತಿದ್ದಂತೆ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ, ಆವಾಸವು ಪೋಷಿಸಬಲ್ಲ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: No population in nature has unlimited resources; this leads to competition among individuals for limited resources, and the "fittest" survive and reproduce. In a habitat, resources can support a maximum possible number beyond which no further growth is possible: this is the carrying capacity (K) for that species in that habitat. A population growing in a habitat with limited resources first shows a lag phase, then phases of acceleration and deceleration, and finally an asymptote, when density reaches K. A plot of N against time gives a sigmoid (S-shaped) curve; this type of growth is called Verhulst–Pearl logistic growth. Since resources for most animal populations are finite sooner or later, the logistic model is considered more realistic.

narration.en: With limited resources, growth follows the logistic equation dN by dt equals rN times K minus N over K. The curve is S-shaped: a lag phase, acceleration, deceleration, and finally an asymptote at the carrying capacity K.
narration.kn: ಸೀಮಿತ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K ಸಮೀಕರಣವನ್ನು ಅನುಸರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆ S-ಆಕಾರ: ವಿಳಂಬ ಹಂತ, ವೇಗವರ್ಧನೆ, ನಿಧಾನಗತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಕೊನೆಗೆ ಧಾರಣ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ K ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರತೆ.

say.en: No habitat has unlimited resources. The logistic equation slows growth as N approaches K, the carrying capacity.
Compare the two curves from the same start: exponential growth keeps rising as a J, while logistic growth bends over and levels off at K as an S.
The S curve has four phases: a lag phase, acceleration, deceleration, and the asymptote at K.
Worked example: r = 0.2 and K = 1000. At N = 500, dN/dt = 0.2 × 500 × 0.5 = 50 per year. At N = 1000 growth stops.

aim.en: To plot the growth curve of a bacterial culture and find its specific growth rate and generation time.

narration.en: Grow a bacterial culture in a flask with limited nutrients and plot the counts. Find the lag phase, the steep exponential phase and the flat stationary phase where the curve levels off, just like the S-shaped logistic curve.

body.en: Populations evolve to maximise their reproductive fitness, also called Darwinian fitness (a high r value), in the habitat in which they live. Under a particular set of selection pressures, organisms evolve towards the most efficient reproductive strategy. Some organisms breed only once in their lifetime (Pacific salmon fish, bamboo), while others breed many times (most birds and mammals). Some produce a large number of small-sized offspring (oysters, pelagic fishes), while others produce a small number of large-sized offspring (birds, mammals). Ecologists suggest that life history traits evolve in relation to the constraints imposed by the abiotic and biotic components of the habitat.

points.en: Breed many times: most birds and mammals
Many small offspring: oysters, pelagic fishes

narration.en: Organisms evolve the reproductive strategy that maximises fitness in their habitat. Pacific salmon and bamboo breed only once; most birds and mammals breed many times. Oysters produce huge numbers of tiny offspring, while birds and mammals produce a few large ones.
narration.kn: ಜೀವಿಗಳು ತಮ್ಮ ಆವಾಸದಲ್ಲಿ ಯೋಗ್ಯತೆಯನ್ನು ಗರಿಷ್ಠಗೊಳಿಸುವ ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ ತಂತ್ರವನ್ನು ವಿಕಾಸಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಪೆಸಿಫಿಕ್ ಸಾಲ್ಮನ್ ಮತ್ತು ಬಿದಿರು ಜೀವನದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಮಾತ್ರ ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ; ಸಿಂಪಿಗಳು ಅನೇಕ ಸಣ್ಣ ಮರಿಗಳನ್ನು, ಪಕ್ಷಿ-ಸಸ್ತನಿಗಳು ಕೆಲವೇ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಮರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಉತ್ಪಾದಿಸುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: A fish population in a lake has r = 0.2 per year and carrying capacity K = 1,000. Find dN/dt when N = 200, N = 500 and N = 1,000.

steps.en: N = 500: 0.2 × 500 × 500/1000 = 50 per year (the maximum, at N = K/2).

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A fish population in a lake has r = 0.2 per year and carrying capacity K = 1,000. Find dN/dt when N = 200, N = 500 and N = 1,000.

body.en: On a logistic curve the population grows fastest at N = K/2, the steepest point of the S. Maximum growth rate = rK/4.

points.en: Limited resources → logistic growth: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K.

points.en: S-curve phases: lag, acceleration, deceleration, asymptote at K.
points.kn: S-ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಯ ಹಂತಗಳು: ವಿಳಂಬ, ವೇಗವರ್ಧನೆ, ನಿಧಾನಗತಿ, K ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರತೆ.

points.en: Life histories vary: breed once or many times; many small or few large offspring.

narration.kn: ಪುನರಾವರ್ತನೆ. ಸೀಮಿತ ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲ → ಲಾಜಿಸ್ಟಿಕ್ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆ: dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K. S-ವಕ್ರರೇಖೆಯ ಹಂತಗಳು: ವಿಳಂಬ, ವೇಗವರ್ಧನೆ, ನಿಧಾನಗತಿ, K ಯಲ್ಲಿ ಸ್ಥಿರತೆ. ಘಾತೀಯ ಮಾದರಿಗಿಂತ ಲಾಜಿಸ್ಟಿಕ್ ಮಾದರಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ವಾಸ್ತವಿಕ. ಜೀವನ ಚರಿತ್ರೆಗಳು ಬೇರೆಬೇರೆ: ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಅಥವಾ ಹಲವು ಬಾರಿ ಸಂತಾನೋತ್ಪತ್ತಿ; ಅನೇಕ ಸಣ್ಣ ಅಥವಾ ಕೆಲವು ದೊಡ್ಡ ಮರಿಗಳು.
